hypothesis: Treating every wrong label as noisy gave no reliable gains. Instead estimate whether the ordinary tree repeatedly under- or over-predicts linked rows, and consider an offset only when that group's tendency repeats in training. Use stored predictions from four genuinely out-of-group teacher fits.
algorithm: Infer recurring-profile and varying-context field blocks on fitting inputs. Form grouping keys from each block and from the recurring-profile key crossed with each varying field of cardinality two to 24. For each grouping estimate the variance of its residual log-odds effects from cross-products of summed residuals in two exact-feature-group halves. Subtract the Bernoulli prediction from the true training outcome, scale using sum of p(1-p), shrink group offsets toward zero and center by training counts. Select the interaction grouping yielding the strongest supported variance contribution on training only. Compare a main-effect offset and a main-plus-one-interaction offset on a tree, reusing the same fitted base and teacher predictions. Two fitted statistical correction layers, no additional base model. Identity for unknown groups.
assessment: Freeze all 2432 development predictions. Compare both against the previous research pair and report the original tree separately. The existing election nominates a fraction on the first 808 and must gain .003 net with nonnegative effects on 817 and 807. Independently report the candidate's standalone differences from the uncorrected original tree on each panel. No result on reused development panels can promote a release by itself.
